title: Precision profile intake: immutable-hashchain, publish workflow, and regression anchors
creator: Ava Martin
description:
Objective: Create a robust intake and publishing workflow for quantization profiles (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) that guarantees artifact immutability, links each profile to a pinned model version, and wires published profiles into a synthetic-regression anchoring system. The system should detect perf regressions early and provide automated guardrails (alerts, controlled rollbacks, and escalations) before profiles are promoted to production routes.

Background: We currently accept quant profiles as blobs with limited provenance and rely on manual CI checks. This yields gaps: (1) hard-to-trace regressions after promotion, (2) no canonical fingerprint tying profile<->model version, (3) limited ability to run economical synthetic anchors across diverse hardware targets.

Success criteria (measurable):
- All incoming quant profiles are stored with an SHA256 immutable fingerprint and signer metadata.
- Published profile artifact includes: fingerprint, model_hash, quant_backend (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8), target_device_profile, sample_inputs_hash, and evaluation-report link.
- Canary harness runs nightly synthetic anchors for promoted profiles for at least 3 representative models/families and 3 device types (A100, H100, L4e).
- Regression detection rule: regressions flagged when >2% drop in mean ROUGE-like perf or >5% increase in tail latency (p99) on synthetic anchors compared to pinned baseline.
- Dashboard panels and automated alerts exist in Console (release: console-2026.03).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Quant Registry API: small service to accept profile uploads, compute fingerprint, validate schema, and persist artifact metadata to registry (S3 + signed manifest).
2) Hashchain & provenance: maintain an append-only manifest per model-version containing profile fingerprints, uploader, CI-check status, and signed approval stamp. Use object signing + manifest chaining to provide immutability audit trail.
3) CI/eval integration: extend existing quant-eval CI to generate an evaluation-report JSON with standard metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput tokens/sec, quality metrics on canonical prompt-set). Persist report link in registry.
4) Canary anchors: a light-weight synthetic workload runner that executes representative prompts and captures telemetry. Anchors are scheduled nightly and on-profile-publish for staged promotion.
5) Rollout and pinflow: UI/API to pin profile to model-version; staged rollouts with weights (0%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with automatic hold/rollback if regression triggers.
6) Observability & alerts: define metric contracts, dashboards, and PagerDuty alerting for regressions.

Acceptance criteria (for ticket completion):
- Registry API endpoints implemented and documented (POST /profiles, GET /profiles/{fingerprint}).
- Upload flow signs manifest and stores evaluation-report link.
- Canary anchor job in k8s + runner that posts summary metrics to telemetry pipeline.
- Console dashboard with baseline vs candidate comparison and automated alerting rule.
- E2E smoke test: upload a test INT8 profile for a small GPT-family model, run canary anchor, validate automatic detection of a purposely-inserted perf delta, and exercise rollback API.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Immutable store: S3 object signatures + manifest hashchain vs. full blockchain-like append-only DB. We chose S3 signatures + manifest chaining to minimize infra maintenance and enable easy customer export.
- Canary sampling frequency vs cost: running anchors per publish is expensive on H100; compromise: run full anchor matrix nightly and lightweight immediate anchors on publish limited to low-cost devices.

Security & compliance notes: All profile artifacts are considered sensitive (may expose model behavior). Encryption-at-rest is required. KMS envelope encryption will be used and access audit logs must be turned on. Security review flagged private-deployment nuances (on-prem HSM integration) — see security review doc.

Rollout timeline:
- Week 1 (this ticket): implement registry + hashing + basic upload flow.
- Week 2: CI/eval integration and evaluation-report plumbing.
- Week 3: Canary runner + telemetry plumbing + console dashboard prototype.
- Week 4: E2E smoke, runbook, and cutover to staged promotion flows.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Quant+Profile+Registry+Design
- Eval schema: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/quant-eval-schema
